meta.purpose: Original style library for generating FTB Quests titles and descriptions. Every example below was invented for this file. Nothing is copied from any modpack, wiki, or song.
meta.register: Playful, confident, short. Puns land once and move on. Facts before flavour. Second person, present tense.

title_patterns.template_hint: Wordplay built on the item's own name or function; the base word must stay recognisable.
examples_original: Grind Over Matter — millstone or any grinding machine
Shaft Happens — kinetic shafts and gearboxes
Pipe Dreams — first fluid or item pipes
Tanks a Lot — fluid tank
Belt It Out — conveyor or mechanical belt
Alloy There! — first alloy ingot
Nugget About It — nugget-tier crafting
Chunk of the Action — chunk loader
A Boring Machine — tunnel bore or mining drill
Gear We Go — first cogwheels or gears
Casing the Joint — machine casings
Sear Pressure — searing or frying station

title_patterns.template_hint: Short declarative gravitas for a tier unlock or first-of-its-kind moment; no joke, let the moment carry it.
examples_original: First Spark — first generator or battery
The Grid Goes Live — first connected energy network
Steel at Last — first steel ingot after a long chain
Ignition — first engine, boiler, or reactor start
The Sky Is Optional — first jetpack or flight item
Critical Mass — nuclear or max-tier reactor
Brass Tacks — mid-tier alloy age unlock
The Quarry Wakes — first automated miner
Endgame Knocks — final tier gate

A Rainbow in Wool — all sixteen wool colours

The Gem Cabinet — all gem types

The Menagerie — capture or tame every mob

title_patterns.template_hint: Either a regal epithet ('Name, Title of Domain') or a short menace line that teases the fight without spoiling it.
examples_original: Vexmara, Mother of Screams — invented epithet for a witch-type boss
The Hollow King — short epithet for an undead ruler
Ashen Tyrant of the Vault — epithet for a nether vault boss
Knock Before Entering — dungeon gatekeeper boss
No Second Chances — one-shot or hardcore arena fight
The Floor Is Lava, Officially — magma arena boss
Bring a Friend or Ten — raid-tier boss
It Was Never Sleeping — awakened ancient horror tease
Cut Off the Head — hydra or multi-phase boss
Last Door on the Left — final dungeon boss

examples_original: Knead to Know — first dough or bread
The Upper Crust — pies and pastries

Rise and Brine — pickled or fermented foods
Grill Seeker — smoker or grill
Butter Late Than Never — churn or butter

examples_original: Strike While the Ingot's Hot — forge or anvil work
A Watched Pot Never Smelts — passive or slow smelter
Measure Twice, Quarry Once — quarry placement
The Early Bird Gets the Wyrm — dragon or wyrm hunt

Don't Count Your Chickens — breeding automation

title_patterns.template_hint: Bare item or system name for steps players will search for; clarity beats cleverness on required recipes.
examples_original: Mechanical Press — required machine, tutorial step

examples_original: Faster. — speed upgrade tier, one word and a full stop

Outrun the Storm — timed event

title_rules: One to four words is the sweet spot; never exceed six words or about 28 characters, or the quest map truncates it.
Title Case everywhere; keep articles and short prepositions lowercase mid-title ('Chunk of the Action').
A bare item name beats a joke whenever the quest is a required crafting step players will Ctrl-F for.
One pun per screen-neighbourhood: two adjacent joke titles cancel each other out.
Never pun where the player arrives frustrated — death recovery, corruption cures, grief repair. Be plain and helpful there.
Bosses get either a regal epithet ('Name, Title of Domain') or a short menace line; never both, never a joke that deflates the fight.
Milestones get gravitas, not gags: short declarative, gold colour code.
Never spoil a boss twist or story beat in a title; tease, don't tell.
Ban 'Obtain X', 'Get X', 'Craft X' as titles — that is what the task icon already says.
Skip the pun when the item name itself is already a joke or too obscure; the reader must recognise the base word instantly.
Keep one naming motif per chapter: all-puns in cooking, all-epithets in the boss gauntlet. Consistency reads as intent.
Punctuation inside titles is a spice: at most one '?' or '!' or trailing '.' per chapter, used for effect ('Faster.').
Spell out numbers under ten unless it is a tier label ('Mk. II', 'Tier 3').
No real brands, songs, memes, or living people — they date the pack and invite takedowns.
A title is a permanent map label: it must still make sense after the quest is done.
desc_rules: Lead with the how-to fact: the first sentence tells the player what to do or where to find it.
Second person, present tense, confident: 'You'll need rotation from above' — never 'the player should'.
One flavour clause maximum, and it comes after the facts, never before them.
If the quest gates progression, say what it unlocks next in one clause: 'This opens the brass line.'
One to three sentences for a normal quest; up to five only for chapter openers.
Colour usage: &e for item and block names, &6 for milestones and key nouns, &7 for optional hints and alternatives, &c for danger warnings, &8&o for a single whispered flavour line.
Return to the body colour immediately after a highlighted word; never let a colour bleed across a sentence.
Hazards get their own short &c sentence — explosion radius, curse effect, void drop — never buried mid-paragraph.
Name the exact interface: the keybind, the GUI tab, the JEI/REI trick. Specificity is the whole value of a questbook.
Never restate the task list ('Collect 3 iron') — write what the icons cannot show: where, why, and the gotcha.
Real numbers build trust: SU, FE/t, seconds, block ranges. Vague adjectives ('powerful', 'useful') build nothing.
Break idea groups with a blank line (\n\n); a wall of text is skipped, and a skipped description is a wasted quest.
Keep lore out of tech chapters; story chapters carry lore, tech chapters get at most one italic &8&o line.
Never say 'simply', 'just', or 'easy' about a step the player might struggle with; respect earns re-reads.
Mark optional or skippable content up front with &7 so completionists and speedrunners can both self-serve.

desc_templates.shape: What it does in plain words, then the one setup fact everyone misses, then an optional &7 tip or what it unlocks.
examples_original:
Presses metal into &esheets&r. It needs rotation from directly above and squashes whatever sits on the belt below it.

&7Sheets feed almost everything in the next row of this chapter.
The &eCrusher&r turns ores into dust at a 1-to-2 ratio — your first free ore doubling. Face the input toward your hopper line or it will spit items on the floor.

Burns any solid fuel into &e40 FE/t&r. It will not push power on its own: run a cable to it or slap a battery on top.

&7Upgrade slots are hidden behind the side tab.

This is your autocrafter. Set the recipe with a &efilter ghost grid&r, feed it from any inventory, and it keeps a stock of whatever you pin.

&8&oIt never sleeps. It never asks why.

desc_templates.shape: Where the fight lives, how to start it, one &c danger line, then the reward tease.
examples_original:
She spawns in the &etower ruin&r west of any swamp village. Place the &eskull idol&r on the altar to begin — the fight starts the moment it clicks in.

&cShe silences potions in phase two. Drink before, not during.

&7Her crown is the only key to the vault below.

Summon it by burning &e4 blighted roots&r in the ritual brazier at full moon. Bring a bow; it spends half the fight airborne.

&cContact damage ignores armour. Do not hug the boss.

The arena is under the &edesert obelisk&r — drop through the false floor. It heals off nearby undead, so clear the room first.

&7Drops the &6Sun Core&r, which starts the solar power line.

Ring the &ecracked bell&r three times and stand back. Phase one is a patience check; phase two is a geometry test.

&cThe shockwave rings outward through walls. Height is safety.

desc_templates.shape: Fastest current source first, one &7 alternate route, then what the material feeds next.
examples_original:
The fastest source right now is &esifting gravel&r — roughly one in four sifts. 

&7A fortune pick on deepslate veins works too, but slower.

You'll want a stack before the alloy furnace shows up.

Melt down &eraw ore&r in the smeltery for double output; each block yields two ingots' worth.

&7The dwarven trader sells it at 3 emeralds if RNG hates you.

This is the backbone of every machine frame in this chapter.

Grows only on &esoul soil&r under a light level of 7 or lower. One farm plot of nine sustains everything this chapter asks for.

&7Bonemeal works on it, but sparingly — it doubles the growth stages too.

Comes off the &eblaze-type mobs&r in the basalt deltas, one or two per kill. Looting helps a lot here.

Six rods fund your first brewing setup and the fire-proofing line after it.

desc_templates.shape: Frame the set as an exhibit, say where the stragglers hide, promise the completion reward.
examples_original:
One of every &esapling&r in the pack — sixteen in all. The last two only drop in the &eflowering grove&r biome, so bring shears and patience.

&6Finishing the set unlocks the arborist's crate.

Every &egem&r gets a slot here. Most come from mining; the odd ones hide in fishing loot and desert temple chests.

&7Check the wandering trader on Tuesdays. Yes, really.

Sixteen colours of &ewool&r, no dye duplication tricks required — flowers cover fourteen of them.

&6Complete the rainbow for a shepherd's bundle and a very smug feeling.

A trophy from each of the five &earena bosses&r. They drop every kill, so a lost trophy just means a rematch.

&6The full shelf opens the champion's chapter.

desc_templates.shape: Portal recipe or ritual first, short packing list, one &c hazard, one line on why to go.
examples_original:
Build a &e4x5 frame of polished basalt&r and light it with the ember lantern. The portal holds for ten minutes per charge.

Bring fire resistance and a stack of cobble.

&cThe floor near spawn-in is unstable. Bridge, don't sprint.

The &evoid key&r drops from the final vault boss — one use, so mark your exit. 

&cNo beds work there. Set a respawn anchor before you jump.

&7Everything that grows there grows nowhere else.

Throw a &eprism shard&r into any deep ocean ritual ring during a storm. The way back is the same ring on the far side.

Pack water breathing, a conduit if you have one, and empty inventory space — you'll want it.

Craft the &efrostgate sigil&r and right-click any intact ice spire. 

&cCold drains hunger twice as fast until you craft lined armour.

&7The natives trade generously if you arrive unarmed.

banned: Title spam of the form 'Obtain X' / 'Get X' / 'Craft X' — the task icon already says it.
'Your first X. More to come.' — filler that promises nothing specific.
'Small step, big payoff' and any other empty aphorism that fits every quest equally.
'Time to...' as a repeated title or opener ('Time to Mine!', 'Time to Cook!').
'Congratulations! You have crafted...' — restating what the player just did.
'This is one of the most important items in the mod.' — says nothing; state the actual use.
'As you progress, you will find...' — vague forward reference with no fact.
'Simply craft...' or 'Just make...' with no location, source, or gotcha attached.
Multiple exclamation points, or an exclamation point on more than a couple of quests per chapter.
'Let's get started!' / 'Let's dive in!' chapter openers.
'Not just X, but Y' rhetorical constructions and chained em-dash asides.
'In this quest, you will...' — the questbook is not a syllabus.
Punning on every single title in a chapter — pun fatigue kills the good ones.
'Good luck!' endings pasted onto every description.
Adjective padding: 'powerful', 'amazing', 'useful', 'essential' with no number or fact behind them.
Copying or lightly rephrasing titles or sentences from existing packs, wikis, or songs.
